My research is about finding structure in complex nonlinear systems and using it to predict them. I
come from computational fluid dynamics and geophysics, and now work mostly at the meeting point of
dynamical systems, data analysis and quantum-mechanical ideas. Papers are listed under
Publications.

### Data-driven modeling and machine learning

Observations of climate, neural activity or turbulent flows are high-dimensional and noisy. I work on
ways to reduce them to a few meaningful spatiotemporal patterns and to use those patterns for
prediction, including extended-range forecasting of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation and the
identification of the Madden–Julian Oscillation.

### Operator-theoretic methods for nonlinear dynamics

Instead of following individual trajectories, operator-theoretic methods study how a system acts on
observables. Koopman operators and their spectra give a linear description of nonlinear dynamics,
which can be learned from data with kernel methods, tensor networks and exterior calculus. I use these
tools to separate trends, cycles and modes of variability in the climate system, and to analyse
non-autonomous and skew-product systems.

### Quantum-mechanical approaches and quantum computing

The same operator framework connects classical dynamics to quantum mechanics. I work on embedding
classical systems in quantum computers, on second quantization of classical nonlinear dynamics, and on
quantum-mechanical closure and data assimilation, where a quantum formalism is used to model the
unresolved scales of a classical system.

### Physics and complex systems

I am a physicist by training, and physics is still how I approach a problem: conserved quantities,
symmetries, the scales on which something happens, and the behaviour that appears once many parts
interact. Complex systems are where that way of thinking is hardest to apply and most useful. The
underlying laws are known in principle, but what one wants to predict lives far from any single scale,
so the task becomes finding the structures that organize the system and building models that keep
them. In my own work this has meant turbulent and multiscale flows, clouds and precipitation,
atmospheric and oceanic variability, plasmas, sea ice, neural activity and stellar oscillations.

### Strategy and decision making

Outside the sciences, I am interested in making strategy and decision making objective: stating what
is actually being optimized, keeping the evidence in view, and being able to defend a choice by
something firmer than intuition. That interest led to my 2025 management thesis at the SGH Warsaw
School of Economics, *Evolutionary Ownership & Machine Learning of Strategy: AI for Modeling Adaptive
Management of Global Mission-Driven Ventures*. What draws me to the subject is the future of
international mission-driven ventures: how they can be owned, governed and steered across borders.
The legal side of this is genuinely complicated, yet technology, and machine learning in particular,
opens up so many possibilities that ambitious dreams and visions now look pursuable at scale.
